subject: Renewal: Dedicated Capacity Increase & Throughput Guarantees (Hyperion AI)

Subject: Renewal conversation — forecast & SLA ask

Hi Logan,

As Hyperion approaches our contract renewal (Jan 31), we'd like to lock in a dedicated pool expansion and a short SLA commitment for peak inference performance. Over the last six months our interface traffic has grown ~2.8x and we expect continued growth driven by Q1 product launches.

Quick high-level asks:
- Increase reserved GPUs to support a sustained 2.5k peak QPS for text-generation (using redwood/gpt-2.7b-like variant) with 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms.
- Option to burst additional capacity during marketing spikes for up to 24 hours.
- Confirmation of token pricing tiers for the larger pool and any minimum-term addendum.

Can you share a recommended GPU plan and rough cost delta so procurement can prep the paperwork?

Thanks,
Eliza
VP Product, Hyperion AI

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Folks — I ran throughput modeling (attached workbook) against Hyperion's August–Nov telemetry and the forecast profile Eliza sent. Summary (short):

- Current baseline (Nov average): 950 QPS, median 60 tokens/request, tail usage to 1.8k QPS during marketing peaks.
- Q1 growth projection: conservative +40% (new feature adoption) to aggressive +95% (product-led viral). We recommend planning for the conservative mid-case +60% to give runway across the term.
- Target 95th-pctl token latency <= 120ms for generation with 512 context. That maps to needing roughly 24x A100-80GB-equivalent GPU throughput under our standard kernel mix for sustained 2.5k QPS in your mid-case.

Recommendation (renewal add-on):
- Reserved pool: increase by 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (can be H100s if Hyperion prefers newer hardware; see pricing delta in the sheet). This yields headroom to 2.8k sustained QPS with autoscale thresholds to 3.6k for short bursts.
- Burst capacity: add a 48-hour burst credit bucket (prepaid) equal to 40% of the reserved pool capacity, usable in 4-hour increments.
- Throughput SLA: 95th-pctl token latency <=120ms for requests routed to the dedicated pool; credit-based remediation (service credits) for sustained outages.

Cost/term notes:
- Incremental reserved capacity line-item + monthly commit; 12x A100-equivalent adds ~ $92k/month on a 12-month term (volume discount applied). Switching to H100 yields ~ +18% on price with ~20% throughput improvement for your model.
- If Hyperion signs a 24-month commitment we can offer a 12% rebate on the committed capacity line.

Attachments: capacity_modeling.xlsx (sheets: input-telemetry, qps-forecasts, gpu-configs, cost-breakdown).

I included a conservative and aggressive sensitivity tab — happy to walk through specific rows in a call.

-Neha
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Eliza Park <eliza@hyperionai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — forecast & SLA ask

Thanks — Neha, this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from procurement before we escalate to legal:
1) The 12 GPU increase — can that be delivered as a mix (8 H100 + 4 A100) to give us some near-term perf improvement while keeping price close to the A100 path?
2) For the burst credit bucket, is there a way to auto-trigger based on an SLO breach or do we have to manually request bursts?
3) For latency remediation, can we add an explicit 99th-pctl target for the control plane (calling/dispatch) separate from token latency for generation?

Also, any chance you can share the per-token blended price once the reserved pool scales (we need that to build the forecast for our CFO).

If these items look reasonable we'll move to a commercial term sheet next week.

—Eliza
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Park <eliza@hyperionai.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, procurement@hyperionai.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — forecast & SLA ask

Eliza — great questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Hybrid pool (8 H100 + 4 A100) — doable. Pricing: hybrid mix priced at +9% vs straight A100 fleet; we factored the H100 perf bump into the throughput headroom in the workbook.
2) Burst automation — we can auto-trigger burst allocations when the pool sustained utilization exceeds 85% for >5 minutes, subject to burst credits remaining. We'll include automation rules in the addendum so it's off by default and configurable.
3) Control-plane 99th-pctl target — we can commit to a 99th-pctl dispatch latency <= 40ms for the dedicated control plane in the addendum; remedies remain service credits.

Per-token blended pricing for the scaled pool (mid-case): generation: $0.00045 / token for committed capacity usage; burst usage billed at $0.00060 / token. These rates are applied post-commit discounts listed in the workbook.

Next steps: I will share a redlined addendum and a draft term sheet (billing lines, commit period, SLA bullets) by Monday. If procurement signs off on the hybrid mix and the 24-month rebate option looks attractive, we can route to legal the week of Dec 14.

Attaching: redwood-dedicated-addendum.pdf (draft), and the capacity_modeling.xlsx workbook for your finance team.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Manager | Redwood Inference
